description: 🤖 We are a team of Cybersecurity, AI and Computing students from UdeG (Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico.), combining technical execution with proven leadership and teamwork. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we leverage machine learning, intelligent data processing, and secure design to solve complex space data problems.
summary:
ARES / ANALOG DISCOVERY is an interactive GIS and AI-powered web platform deployed on AWS Amplify that discovers and ranks terrestrial analogs for permanent lunar bases and Martian landing sites.

How it addresses the challenge: Instead of relying on static visual comparisons in overused locations, ARES integrates NASA GIBS satellite layers, NASA Earthdata, and Planetary Data System (PDS) metrics across 12 monthly seasonal windows. Users select a planetary target—such as Jezero Crater (Mars 2020)—and dynamically customize nine Similarity Weights divided into Analog Fidelity and Base & Launch Operations. Our deterministic algorithm penalizes missing data and ranks global basins in real time (e.g., identifying Mexico's Laguna Alchichica at 84.3% and Cuatro Ciénegas at 83.2% ahead of traditional sites like Atacama at 60.2%), complemented by the ASK ARES AI assistant and mandatory "Analogy Limits" metadata.

Why it is important: ARES reduces mission testing risks, prevents cognitive bias, safeguards fragile extremophile ecosystems, and decentralizes planetary research worldwide.
details:
ARES (Planetary Analog Temporal Discovery Engine) is a geospatial and temporal discovery engine that identifies where on Earth—and during which exact month of the year—an endorheic (closed) basin most accurately replicates the physical, thermal, topographic, and mineralogical conditions of exploration sites on Mars and the Moon. Rather than treating terrestrial analogs as static locations, ARES models the monthly seasonal dynamics of 56 global endorheic basins, evaluating 672 basin-month windows (56 basins × 12 months).

  • Multi-Source Earth Observation Pipeline: ARES integrates daily/monthly climatology from the NASA POWER API (diurnal temperature range $\Delta T$, precipitation, surface wind speed, relative humidity, and solar irradiance) normalized into indices for aridity, thermal shock, and aeolian dust activity. It combines this with terrain elevation and slope derived from the Copernicus DEM around each basin's lacustrine or salt-flat core, plus hyperspectral orbital mineralogy from ISS EMIT L2BMIN (processed via NASA AppEEARS through merge_appeears.py) alongside literature-backed baseline mineral profiles.
  • Multi-Variable Planetary Similarity Engine (build_engine.py): The engine calculates a 0%–100% similarity score using weighted Euclidean distance across five normalized physical dimensions—aridity, diurnal thermal contrast, dust activity, topographic slope, and mineralogical affinity. Each terrestrial window is evaluated against five mission sites: Jezero Crater, Gale Crater (Aeolis Palus), Meridiani Planum, and Eberswalde Paleolake on Mars, as well as Shackleton Rim at the lunar south pole.
  • Interactive Mission Dashboard (frontend/index.html): Users explore the 56 basins on an interactive global map color-coded by similarity score, toggle adjustable topographic overlays (OpenTopoMap, Esri Hillshade 3D, and Esri World Topo) with a 0%–100% opacity slider, switch between Auto-Discovery (which automatically finds each basin's peak similarity month) and single-month filtering, calibrate physical variable weights in real time, and inspect 12-month dual-axis charts comparing planetary similarity (%) against diurnal temperature range ($\Delta T$ in °C).

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Precision Field-Campaign Planning: ARES helps planetary scientists, astrobiologists, and rover engineering teams pinpoint not only the best terrestrial analog site for a specific mission target, but also the exact seasonal window when local aridity, wind, and thermal cycling peak in planetary fidelity.
  • Zero-Server Portability: By separating scientific computation in Python from browser visualization and exporting precompiled data payloads (analogs_data.js and analogs_data.json), the platform runs instantaneously in any standard web browser without requiring dedicated backend servers or complex runtime dependencies.
  • Extensible Mission Architecture: Researchers can add new planetary targets, incorporate rover surface telemetry (such as Perseverance MEDA or Curiosity REMS), or integrate newly processed ISS EMIT spectral CSVs simply by dropping files into data/raw/appeears/ and re-running the Python pipeline.

Creativity & Factors Considered

  • Time as a Primary Discovery Variable: Conventional terrestrial analog catalogs assume a desert or salt flat resembles Mars or the Moon year-round. ARES introduces seasonal temporality—showing how monsoons, seasonal desiccation, wind regimes, and diurnal thermal swings cause a basin's planetary similarity to rise and fall across the calendar year.
  • Target-Specific Mineralogical Weighting: Our team modeled distinct mineralogical affinity vectors tailored to the geology of each target—prioritizing carbonates and phyllosilicates (smectites) for Jezero Crater and Eberswalde Paleolake, hydrated sulfates and crystalline hematite for Meridiani Planum and Gale Crater, and extreme hyper-aridity, severe thermal shock, and steep crater-rim slopes for Shackleton Rim.
  • Field-Ready Offline Resilience: We structured the frontend to load precompiled JavaScript datasets directly via <script> tags, preventing local browser CORS blocks so teams can deploy and use the tool even in low-connectivity environments.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software

  • Programming Languages: Python (3.9+), HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript.
  • Python Libraries & Storage Formats: pandas, pyarrow, numpy, requests, Apache Parquet (basins_base.parquet), and JSON.
  • Frontend & Visualization Libraries: Leaflet.js (with CARTO dark basemaps, OpenTopoMap, Esri World Hillshade, and Esri World Topo tile layers) and Chart.js.
  • NASA & Open Earth Data Sources: NASA POWER API, Copernicus DEM, and ISS EMIT L2BMIN via NASA AppEEARS.
